CVX.rationale: CVX is a strong franchise (39-year dividend streak, integrated model, Hess-acquired Gulf of America scale, Project Kilby optionality) but the fundamental trajectory is sharply negative and the valuation is the most stretched in the 1-year window. Q1 2026 EPS collapsed 44.5% YoY to $1.11, operating cash flow cratered 73% QoQ to $2.51B, and net income fell 34.7% — all driven by the WTI crash from $114.58 to $69.73 (-39.1% in three months). Despite this earnings deterioration, the P/E has nearly doubled from ~16x to ~29.8x, sitting near the top of its 1-year range. The earnings yield of 3.4% is below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.49%, meaning investors are being paid less to own a cyclical energy stock than risk-free bonds. The balance sheet is deteriorating (equity down, liabilities up) post-Hess acquisition, and multiple sources flag the dividend is 'not fully backed by earnings or free cash flow.' Management itself warns that 'prices don't reflect true industry fundamentals.' There is no near-term catalyst to re-rate the stock higher — Q2 earnings (July 31) are likely to reflect the full weight of the oil-price collapse, and the Project Kilby deal, while strategically interesting, is modest relative to company scale and years from cash flow. The combination of collapsing fundamentals, stretched valuation, negative equity risk premium, and a deteriorating commodity backdrop makes CVX extremely unattractive at this juncture.
